explanation: Dereferencing a null pointer in C occurs when you attempt to access or modify the memory location pointed to by a pointer that has a value of NULL (typically 0). This is problematic because NULL does not point to a valid memory address, leading to undefined behavior such as a segmentation fault. It is used to highlight memory safety issues in C programming, helping developers detect and prevent bugs related to invalid memory access, as operating systems often protect low memory addresses (like page 0) to catch such errors.
